subject: Significantly different latent means/intercepts but no difference in factor scores between groups

messages.author: 234887487104942e
messages.subject: Significantly different latent means/intercepts but no difference in factor scores between groups
parts:
Hello,

I have a good-fitting mutliple-group (2 groups total) model with equal loadings and intercepts across groups (scalar measurement invariance). The latent mean/intercept of the first group is set to zero (for identification purposes) and the latent intercept of the second group is significantly different from zero:

                  Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|) ci.lower ci.upper   Std.lv  Std.all
   LV                0.971    0.048   20.071    0.000    0.876    1.066    1.000    1.000

However, the difference between the mean factor scores of both groups, extracted with the lavPredict() function, is nearly zero (-0,04).
Does this result make sense?

I will appreciate any answer/explanation.

messages.author: 234887487104942e
messages.subject: Re: Significantly different latent means/intercepts but no difference in factor scores between groups
parts: In other words, factor scores derived from multiple-group models with equal items' intercepts and loadings are always centered around zero in each group. Is this a normal result?
